gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 7?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Official observations from the German Weather Service will resolve the market once final readings are confirmed. Unexpected shifts such as increased cloud cover, localized showers, or revisions in the final model runs could still alter the measured maximum.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency project a maximum of 35°C for Tokyo on August 8 under partly cloudy skies, yet trader consensus clusters tightly around 33–34°C amid model spreads in sea-breeze timing and afternoon cloud development that can shave 1–2°C from peak readings. High humidity near 70–80% and the urban heat island effect amplify apparent temperatures, but variable wind patterns and any earlier marine layer intrusion often cap actual maxima below guidance. Historical August baselines average 30–32°C, so the narrow 33–34°C band reflects ongoing uncertainty in short-term convective inhibition and observational updates before the daily close.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble model runs for August 9 point to a partly cloudy day with ample afternoon insolation, supporting peak temperatures near the seasonal average of 31–32 °C while allowing modest exceedance under sustained clear conditions. The tight spread between the 32 °C and 33 °C contracts captures uncertainty in cloud timing, boundary-layer mixing, and the urban heat-island enhancement typical of central Tokyo stations. Light steering winds and high humidity limit rapid intensification, yet any delay in afternoon convection could add 1 °C; conversely, scattered showers would cap readings near 32 °C. Traders are therefore weighting the most probable narrow range consistent with official forecast thresholds and historical August variability.
